headings.title: Public policy favoring open government and liberal construction
headings.reviewNote: Declares state public policy that governmental meetings, records, and votes be open, requiring liberal construction of open records and strict construction of exemptions.

headings.title: General requirement for open meetings, records, and votes
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that all public meetings, records, and votes of governmental bodies remain open for public inspection and copying except as provided by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.011 covering public policy favoring open government with liberal construction and general openness of meetings, records, and votes (L. 1987 S.B. 2, A.L. 2004 S.B. 1020, et al.).

headings.title: Notice requirements and public agenda contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires public governmental bodies to give reasonable advance notice of meeting time, date, place, tentative agenda, and electronic access instructions.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour notice deadline and accessible locations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates at least twenty-four hours notice prior to meetings and requires meetings to be held at times and locations reasonably accessible to the public and disabled individuals.

headings.title: Right to record open meetings and guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires public bodies to allow electronic recording of open meetings (with permissive disruption-minimizing guidelines) and prohibits unpermitted audio recording of closed meetings, records, or votes as a class C misdemeanor.

headings.title: Good cause justification for departed notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires the nature of good cause justifying meeting on less than twenty-four hours notice or at inconvenient times to be recorded in the official minutes.

headings.title: Meeting notice exception for formally constituted subunits
headings.reviewNote: Allows subunits to meet without separate notice during parent body recesses if publicly announced and topics coincide with parent body business.

headings.title: Preservation of other specific statutory notice provisions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that specific statutory notice provisions requiring longer notice or specific publications shall control over general Sunshine Law requirements.

headings.title: Journal and minute keeping requirements for meetings
headings.reviewNote: Mandates keeping journals or minutes of open and closed meetings, including date, time, members present, votes taken, and roll call tallies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 610.020 covering meeting notice and agenda rules, 24-hour deadline and accessibility, recording open meetings and class C misdemeanor ban on unauthorized closed recording, good-cause minutes, subunit notice exception, other notice laws, and minutes/roll-call retention (L. 1973 S.B. 1 § 3 through A.L. 2004 S.B. 1020, et al.).

headings.title: Roll call vote and citation to close
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits closing meetings, records, or votes without a recorded roll call vote citing the specific statutory exemption in section 610.021.

headings.title: Advance notice of closed meetings and cited reasons
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice of closed meetings to cite the specific statutory exemption and limits closed business strictly to matters directly related to the cited reason.

headings.title: Limitation of closed discussion to cited exemption
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public bodies from discussing unannounced subjects or taking actions not authorized by the specific cited statutory exemption.

headings.title: Closed meetings, records, or votes not required
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in sections 610.010 to 610.028 requires a public governmental body to hold a closed meeting, record, or vote.

headings.title: Public records presumed open unless exempt
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that public records are presumed open unless otherwise exempt under chapter 610.

headings.title: Member objection to unlawful closure and defense
headings.reviewNote: Directs a member believing a closure motion violates chapter 610 to state an objection entered in the minutes, permits full participation, and grants an absolute defense to section 610.027 claims if the member also voted against closure.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 610.022 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 4 through 6) covering roll-call vote to close, advance closed-meeting notice, topic and space limitations, non-mandatory closure rule, open-record presumption, and member objection defense (L. 1987 S.B. 2 through A.L. 2004 S.B. 1020, et al.; annotation notes Kansas City Star Co. v. Fulson).

headings.title: Redaction of exempt material and open portions
headings.reviewNote: Requires public governmental bodies to separate and redact closed information and make all nonexempt portions of public records available for inspection.

headings.title: Record design and general description of exempt material
headings.reviewNote: Requires public bodies to design records to facilitate separation where practicable and to generally describe readily apparent exempted material unless doing so would reveal exempt contents and defeat the exemption.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.024 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2) covering separation of exempt and nonexempt record material and record design with general description of readily apparent exemptions (L. 1993 H.B. 170).

headings.title: Copying fees and search cost limitations
headings.reviewNote: Limits fees for paper copies to ten cents per page, permits reasonable staff research costs at average hourly rates, and authorizes electronic duplication charges.

headings.title: Advance fee payment and withdrawal of unanswered requests
headings.reviewNote: Permits requesting fee payment in advance and deems requests withdrawn if fees or clarification responses are not provided within 90 days (or 150 days if fees exceed $1,000), with six-month repeat-request fee rules, a Jan. 1, 2026 deadline for pending Aug. 28, 2025 requests, and a lawsuit exception.

headings.title: State agency remittance to general revenue fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs each state public governmental body, except as otherwise provided by law, to remit fee moneys to the director of revenue for deposit in the state general revenue fund.

headings.title: Political subdivision remittance to fiscal officer
headings.reviewNote: Directs each political subdivision public governmental body, except as otherwise provided by law, to remit fee moneys to its appropriate fiscal officer for deposit in the body's accounts.

headings.title: Exclusion of copying fees from Hancock Amendment
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that copying charges and related fees not exceeding cost recovery for services existing on or voter-approved after November 4, 1980 are not a 'tax, license or fees' under Missouri Constitution Article X, Section 22.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 610.026 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 through 5 and updated history to A.L. 2025 H.B. 145 & 59) covering copying/research fee caps and public interest waivers, advance payment and 90/150-day withdrawal rules, state and political subdivision fee remittances, and Hancock Amendment exclusion (annotation notes Gross v. Parson).

headings.title: Judicial enforcement actions for Sunshine Law violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved persons, prosecuting attorneys, or the attorney general to file circuit court lawsuits to enforce Sunshine Law compliance.

headings.title: Burden of persuasion on public governmental body
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of persuasion on the public governmental body and its members to demonstrate compliance once a plaintiff shows the body is subject to sections 610.010 to 610.026 and held a closed meeting, record, or vote.

headings.title: Civil penalties for knowing violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil fines up to one thousand dollars and discretionary attorney fee awards upon proving a knowing violation by a preponderance of evidence.

headings.title: Enhanced penalties for purposeful violations
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalties up to five thousand dollars and mandatory attorney fees upon proving a purposeful violation by a preponderance of the evidence.

headings.title: Voiding unlawful actions and filing deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Directs courts to void actions taken in violation if the public interest in enforcement outweighs sustaining validity, requires filing within one year of ascertainability and no later than two years after violation, and exempts certain bond actions.

headings.title: Declaratory suit or opinion when legality in doubt
headings.reviewNote: Permits a public governmental body in doubt about closing a meeting, record, or vote to bring a circuit court suit at its own expense or seek a formal opinion from the attorney general or its own attorney.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 610.027 (rewrote shifted subsections 2, 5, and 6) covering judicial enforcement and record preservation, body's burden of persuasion, civil penalties for knowing (up to $1,000) and purposeful (up to $5,000) violations, voiding actions with 1/2-year deadlines, and declaratory suits or opinions (L. 1982 H.B. 1253 through A.L. 2004 S.B. 1020, et al.).

headings.title: Legal defense provided to public body members
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public governmental bodies to provide legal counsel and pay defense costs for members sued in official capacities under open meetings laws.

headings.title: Mandatory written open records and release policy
headings.reviewNote: Obligates every public governmental body to adopt a formal written policy governing public records access, retention, and release.

headings.title: Whistleblower protection against employee retaliation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits dismissing, disciplining, or retaliating against public employees who report alleged Sunshine Law violations in good faith.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 610.028 (corrected enactment history to L. 1982 H.B. 1253, A.L. 1987 S.B. 2, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1548) covering optional member legal defense, mandatory written release policy with compliance immunity, and good-faith reporter protection.

headings.title: Electronic public records access and commercial contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public bodies to provide records electronically and enter into database agreements, provided commercial contracts do not restrict public access.

headings.title: Required security and liability provisions in electronic contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires public governmental bodies to include provisions in electronic services contracts protecting information system security and integrity and limiting the body's liability.

headings.title: Consultation with state data processing division
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state agencies and local governments to consult with the state information technology division regarding electronic database contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 610.029 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2 and updated history through 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision) covering electronic records access and database contract limits, required security and liability contract provisions, and ITSD consultation.

headings.title: Disclosure of closed records for executive investigations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits an executive agency from disclosing identifying information from closed records unless necessary for a requesting executive agency's official constitutional or statutory duties or otherwise required by law.

headings.title: Written request and confidentiality certification
headings.reviewNote: Permits disclosure notwithstanding other laws including section 32.057, while authorizing the providing agency to require written statements of duties, recipient identities, use affirmation, and start date for continuous access.

headings.title: Request retention and one-year continuous access limit
headings.reviewNote: Requires the providing agency to keep the request on file, release only to listed persons, honor continuous-access requests for one year, and require an updated request after expiration.

headings.title: Confidentiality standards and misuse penalties
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any person receiving or releasing closed information under this section to the providing agency's confidentiality and misuse laws, regulations, standards, and penalties.

headings.title: Definition of executive agency
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'executive agency' as any executive branch administrative governmental entity created by Missouri Constitution or statutes, including public higher-education boards, subdivisions, and legally designated agents.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 610.032 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 3 through 5) covering restricted executive agency disclosure of closed records, optional written request conditions (notwithstanding § 32.057), request retention and one-year continuous access limit, confidentiality/misuse penalties, and executive agency definition (L. 1994 S.B. 685; effective 5-10-94).

headings.title: Definitions of arrest, incident, and investigative reports
headings.reviewNote: Defines arrest, arrest report, incident report, investigative report, inactive investigation, and mobile video recordings for law enforcement records.

headings.title: Public accessibility of daily logs and arrest reports
headings.reviewNote: Mandates maintaining open incident and arrest reports, closes investigative reports, mobile video recordings, and public health lab records until inactive, closes uncharged arrest reports after 30 days (except disposition), and authorizes closing nonpublic-location mobile videos subject to depicted-person access.

headings.title: Mandatory redaction for safety or investigation jeopardy
headings.reviewNote: Requires closing and redacting portions of otherwise open law enforcement records (other than arrest reports) likely to pose a clear and present danger to safety, jeopardize an investigation, identify confidential sources or unarrested suspects, or disclose investigative techniques.

headings.title: Access to closed records for civil claims or defenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits involved persons, families, attorneys, or insurers to obtain closed records and unaltered incident reports for civil claims or defenses, requiring agency production or a circuit court motion within 30 days.

headings.title: Judicial action to disclose investigative reports or video
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit court actions to disclose closed investigative reports or mobile video recordings under statutory balancing tests, in camera review, protective orders, and fee-shifting standards.

headings.title: Civil penalties for knowing and purposeful noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalties against law enforcement agencies for knowing or purposeful withholding of required incident logs and arrest records.

headings.title: Confidentiality of chapter 566 sexual offense victim identity
headings.reviewNote: Permits a victim of a chapter 566 offense to request that his or her identity be kept confidential until a charge relating to the incident is filed.

headings.title: Ten-day notice before displaying nonpublic mobile video
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits recipients of nonpublic-location mobile video recordings from displaying or disclosing them without direct notice to depicted non-law-enforcement individuals and at least ten days to seek an injunction, with civil damages for noncompliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 610.100 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 3–5, 7, and 8) covering law enforcement record definitions, open incident/arrest reports and closed active investigative/video records, safety/investigation redactions, civil-claim access, judicial disclosure actions and fee shifting, open-report enforcement penalties, ch. 566 victim identity confidentiality, and 10-day third-party notice before displaying nonpublic video (L. 1973 S.B. 1 § 6 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 1682).

headings.title: Closure of records upon dismissal or suspended sentence
headings.reviewNote: Directs official records of arrest and prosecution to be closed if charges are nolle prossed, dismissed, or a suspended sentence is successfully completed.

headings.title: Disclosure of closed records to crime victims
headings.reviewNote: Requires making closed official records available upon request to the victim (or minor victim's parents/guardian) for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding when imposition of sentence is suspended for specified chapter 566, 568, or 573 offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.105 (tightened subsection 2 note and enactment history) covering closure upon nolle pros, dismissal, acquittal, suspended imposition of sentence, or mental disease acquittal, and victim access in specified suspended-imposition cases (L. 1973 S.B. 1 § 7 through A.L. 2006 H.B. 1053; footnote notes 2014 transfer of §§ 568.080/568.090 to §§ 573.200/573.205).

headings.title: Confidentiality of closed arrest and prosecution records
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that closed records remain inaccessible to the public, restricting disclosure to law enforcement, courts, prosecutors, and state licensing boards.

headings.title: Access limits, identification, and record segregation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts closed record release strictly to listed purposes and entities, permits requiring positive fingerprint identification, governs repository dissemination under section 43.509, and mandates removing, rewriting, or blacking out closed records into separate confidential files.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.120 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2 and updated history to A.L. 2021 S.B. 53 & 60) covering closed record preservation and authorized agency access, plus purpose limits, fingerprint verification, repository dissemination, and record segregation/redaction.

headings.title: Statutory grounds and criteria for arrest expungement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes expunging arrest records based on false information, lack of probable cause, nolle pros of misdemeanor moving violations, or absence of charges.

headings.title: Absence of pending civil litigation requirement
headings.reviewNote: Conditions arrest record expungement eligibility upon the absence of any pending civil action relating to the arrest or records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.122 covering arrest record expungement grounds (false information or dismissed/acquitted non-intoxication chapter 303/moving violations for non-CDL drivers) and absence of pending civil actions (L. 1993 H.B. 170 § 1 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 53 & 60; annotation notes In re Dyer).

headings.title: Verified petition for expungement contents and filing
headings.reviewNote: Sets petition requirements including petitioner demographics, arrest details, charging court, and standard fingerprint cards for central repository matching.

headings.title: Mandatory joinder of possessing agencies as defendants
headings.reviewNote: Requires naming all law enforcement agencies, courts, and central depositories possessing arrest records as party defendants.

headings.title: Hearing schedule and thirty-day notice requirement
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to schedule a hearing no sooner than thirty days after petition filing with reasonable notice to all named defendants.

headings.title: Entry of expungement order and file confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Directs entry of expungement orders upon qualifying findings, making proceeding files confidential and serving orders on all defendant agencies.

headings.title: Supreme court rulemaking and small claims procedure
headings.reviewNote: Directs the supreme court to promulgate rules for handling expungement cases patterned after chapter 482 small claims procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 610.123 covering verified arrest expungement petition contents, mandatory defendant joinder, 30-day minimum hearing schedule, expungement order and file confidentiality, and supreme court small-claims-style rulemaking (L. 1993 H.B. 170 § 2 through A.L. 2005 S.B. 422).

headings.title: Physical destruction, blacking out, and electronic deletion
headings.reviewNote: Mandates physical destruction or blacking out of expunged records, electronic database deletion, and submission of expungement requests to the FBI.

headings.title: Right of appeal by petitioner or agency
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes petitioners and protesting law enforcement agencies to appeal expungement decisions in the manner provided for civil appeals.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.124 covering physical destruction or blacking out, electronic removal, FBI expungement request, and civil appeal rights (L. 1993 H.B. 170 § 3 merged with H.B. 562 § 13).

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for failure to expunge records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly failing to obliterate or unlawfully releasing records subject to an expungement order as a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Felony penalty for using expunged records for gain
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly using expunged arrest information for financial gain as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.125 covering class B misdemeanor for knowingly failing to expunge or releasing expunged arrest information and class E felony for using expunged information for financial gain (L. 1993 H.B. 170 § 4 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Validity of arrest unaffected by expungement
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that arrest record expungement does not invalidate the original arrest or establish a lack of probable cause.

headings.title: Inherent court authority to close records limited
headings.reviewNote: Restricts judicial authority to close or expunge arrest records strictly to powers granted under sections 610.122 to 610.126.

headings.title: Prohibition against subsequent civil lawsuits by petitioner
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits petitioners from bringing subsequent civil actions against any agency or person relating to expunged arrests.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 610.126 covering preservation of arrest validity, statutory limitation on judicial closure/expungement authority, and bar on subsequent petitioner civil actions (L. 1993 H.B. 170 § 5, A.L. 1995 H.B. 135 merged with H.B. 174, et al.).

headings.title: Eligibility criteria for ten-year driving expungement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individuals to apply to expunge a first non-commercial misdemeanor driving or boating intoxication offense after ten conviction-free years.

headings.title: Judicial hearing and required non-recidivism findings
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to enter an expungement order upon finding no subsequent alcohol contacts, convictions, or pending enforcement actions.

headings.title: Confidentiality of records and restoration of legal status
headings.reviewNote: Restores the petitioner to pre-arrest legal status, protects confidentiality of records, and prohibits finding perjury for failing to acknowledge expunged arrests.

headings.title: Exclusion of commercial driver's license holders
headings.reviewNote: Excludes any individual who has been issued or is required to possess a commercial driver's license from this state or any other state.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 610.130 covering ten-year first intoxication-related traffic/boating misdemeanor expungement eligibility, hearing and findings, file confidentiality, status restoration, and single-expungement limit, plus CDL exclusion (L. 1989 1st Ex. Sess. H.B. 3 § 2 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 577.054; effective 1-01-17; annotation notes S.S. v. Mitchell).

headings.title: Expungement of prostitution offenses committed under coercion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a person who pled guilty to or was convicted of prostitution under section 567.020 to apply for expungement, directing the court to order expungement upon finding the person acted under coercion as defined in section 566.200.

headings.title: File confidentiality, status restoration, and perjury immunity
headings.reviewNote: Makes expungement proceeding records confidential, restores the petitioner to pre-arrest legal status, and bars perjury or false statement liability and inquiries regarding the expunged offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.131 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2, tightened subsection 1, and updated history to A.L. 2026 H.B. 2273, et al.) covering prostitution conviction expungement for coercion under section 566.200 and file confidentiality, status restoration, and perjury immunity.

headings.title: Definitions of court, crime, and prosecutor
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'court', 'crime', and 'prosecutor' or 'prosecuting attorney' for purposes of section 610.140.

headings.title: Petition authorization and related same-course crimes
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes petitioning to expunge one or more eligible Missouri crimes and provides that related crimes from the same course of criminal conduct count only as the highest level for eligibility limits.

headings.title: Crimes ineligible for expungement
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates eleven categories of ineligible crimes—including class A felonies, dangerous felonies, sex-offender-registration offenses, death-element felonies, felony/domestic assault, kidnapping, listed statutory offenses, DWI/BWI, CDL traffic violations, and most section 571.030 offenses (footnotes note repealed § 569.067 and transferred § 569.072).

headings.title: Joinder of named law enforcement and court defendants
headings.reviewNote: Requires naming all agencies, courts, and central repositories holding conviction records as party defendants.

headings.title: Required information in expungement petition
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required petition details including petitioner biographical data, each crime sought to be expunged, approximate charge dates, counties/municipalities, and case numbers and court names.

headings.title: Prosecutor notice, hearing, criteria, and rebuttable presumption
headings.reviewNote: Directs clerk notice to the prosecutor, 30-day written objection period, 60-day hearing deadline, six eligibility criteria (including 3-year felony / 1-year misdemeanor waiting periods), rebuttable presumption, and victim right to be heard.

headings.title: Eighteen-month expungement for uncharged arrests
headings.reviewNote: Permits petitioning to expunge arrest records for an eligible crime at least eighteen months after arrest if the petitioner has not been charged and has no misdemeanor or felony findings of guilt during that time.

headings.title: Expungement order deadline, record closure, and FBI request
headings.reviewNote: Requires an expungement or dismissal order within six months of filing, directs entities to close records under section 610.120, makes proceeding files confidential, and directs the central repository to request FBI expungement.

headings.title: Restoration of civil rights and perjury immunity
headings.reviewNote: Restores restricted civil rights (including voting, public office, and jury service), treats expungement as complete removal for 18 U.S.C. 921(a)(33)(B)(ii), grants perjury immunity except for court/subsequent-charge disclosures, and allows prior-offense sentencing use.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosures for licensing and specified employment
headings.reviewNote: Requires disclosing expunged crimes on applications for professional licenses, chapter 313/571 licenses/permits, gaming/lottery/emergency services/law enforcement, federally insured banks, insurers, or legally restricted employers, with employer notice and disqualification rules.

headings.title: Permissible denial on employer inquiries and exception
headings.reviewNote: Permits answering 'no' to employer criminal history inquiries when no public record remains, except requiring affirmative disclosure where federal or state law mandates excluding convicted applicants.

headings.title: Dismissal of petition and one-year refiling bar
headings.reviewNote: Requires dismissing petitions failing statutory criteria or containing knowingly false information and bars refiling for one year after the previous filing date.

headings.title: Lifetime expungement limits and criminal justice access
headings.reviewNote: Caps lifetime expungements at three misdemeanors/ordinance violations with imprisonment and two felonies (with unlimited infractions), while preserving law enforcement and prosecutorial use of expunged records as prior crimes.

headings.title: Pro se expungement petition form and perjury declaration
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to make available a pro se expungement form containing the required declaration under penalty of perjury.

headings.title: Availability of expungement under other laws
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section limits or restricts the availability of expungement under any other law.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 15 subsection headings for 610.140 (rewrote 13 shifted/fabricated subsections to match source text) covering definitions, multi-crime and same-course petitions, excluded offenses (with footnotes on §§ 569.067/569.072), defendants, petition contents, prosecutor notice/hearing/criteria, 18-month arrest expungement, 6-month order/closure/FBI request, rights restoration, mandatory disclosures, employer inquiry rules, dismissal/refiling bar, lifetime limits (3 misdemeanors, 2 felonies), pro se form, and other expungement laws (L. 2012 H.B. 1647 through A.L. 2024 S.B. 754, et al.; effective 1-01-25).

headings.title: Definitions for automatic expungement
headings.reviewNote: Defines case record, criminal history record information, eligible offense, expungement, final disposition, qualifying offense (controlled substance possession and drug paraphernalia under §§ 195.202, 195.233, 579.015, 579.074), and restoration of rights.

headings.title: Automatic expungement and retroactive applicability
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all eligible offenses are automatically expunged as a matter of law upon eligibility, applies retroactively to electronic records regardless of date, and results in record closure and restoration of rights.

headings.title: Weekly central repository screening and supreme court report
headings.reviewNote: Directs the central repository to screen the criminal history database at least weekly, automatically expunge eligible offenses via MULES, rerun analysis upon new data, and report weekly changes to the Missouri Supreme Court.

headings.title: Notification and case record closure by OSCA
headings.reviewNote: Directs the central repository to notify the office of state courts administrator of eligible designations, makes statewide court automation case records confidential, and directs OSCA to expunge case records based on system data and designations.

headings.title: Closed investigative reports and MULES query defense
headings.reviewNote: Requires agencies releasing investigative reports under chapter 610 to treat information relating only to an automatically expunged offense as closed, with an affirmative defense for adhering to a MULES query.

headings.title: Combined lifetime limits on expungements
headings.reviewNote: Limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements combined under sections 610.141 and 610.140, counting only the highest-level offense in multi-offense cases.

headings.title: Preservation of expungement petitions under other law
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section prohibits filing an expungement petition under any other permissible provision of law.

headings.title: Sole remedy for failure to automatically expunge
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the sole remedy for failure to expunge under this section is filing an expungement petition under section 610.140.

headings.title: Annual highway patrol statistical report to legislature
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Missouri State Highway Patrol, beginning January 1, 2028, to submit annual statistical reports on automatic expungements by circuit, county, demographics, and offense type to designated legislative judiciary committees.

headings.title: Contingent effective date no later than 2027
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section takes effect when technically feasible for both OSCA and the central repository, but no later than January 1, 2027.

headings.title: Expungement data sharing with consumer reporting agencies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Missouri State Highway Patrol, notwithstanding section 610.120, to provide requesting consumer reporting agencies with identifying data to delete expunged records under signed compliance and destruction agreements.

headings.title: Informational document provided at sentencing or release
headings.reviewNote: Directs OSCA, the department of corrections, and the highway patrol to jointly develop an expungement informational document provided at sentencing or upon probation/parole release for qualifying offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 subsection headings for 610.141 (rewrote all 12 shifted/fabricated subsections and corrected enactment citation to L. 2026 S.B. 1421) covering definitions, retroactive automatic expungement, weekly repository screening, OSCA case closure, investigative report compliance, combined 3-misdemeanor/2-felony limits, sole remedy, annual reports starting 2028, contingent 2027 effective date, CRA data sharing, and sentencing/release notice (severability § 1.1010).

headings.title: Reporting restrictions for pardoned or expunged records
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits reporting records of arrests, pending indictments, or convictions once it is learned that a full pardon or expungement was granted or that an arrest or indictment did not result in conviction.

headings.title: Attorney general injunctive actions, damages, and fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general to seek injunctions, resident damages under 15 U.S.C. 1681s or up to $1,000 per willful or negligent violation, and mandatory costs and reasonable attorney fees in successful actions.

headings.title: Consumer injunctive relief for violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes injunctive relief available to any consumer aggrieved by a violation or threatened violation of this section regardless of whether other remedies are sought.

headings.title: Liability immunity for employers, volunteer groups, and landlords
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity to employers, volunteer organizations, and landlords for misconduct claims relating to expunged criminal history unless they failed to exercise reasonable care in determining the employee poses no danger or risk.

headings.title: Disclosures required for law enforcement and sensitive employment
headings.reviewNote: Requires disclosing an expunged offense when necessary to complete an employment application for federally insured banks/credit unions, insurers under 18 U.S.C. 1033/1034, or entities authorized to receive closed records under section 610.120.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 610.143 (rewrote inaccurate subsections 2–4 and corrected enactment citation to L. 2026 S.B. 1421) covering non-reporting of pardoned, expunged, or non-conviction records, attorney general remedies and $1,000/violation damages, consumer injunctive relief, employer/volunteer/landlord immunity, and mandatory employment disclosures (severability § 1.1010).

headings.title: Missouri expungement fund creation and administration
headings.reviewNote: Creates the dedicated Missouri Expungement Fund in the state treasury with state treasurer custody, disbursement approval under sections 30.170 and 30.180, and investment earnings credited to the fund.

headings.title: Authorized fund expenditures for IT and personnel
headings.reviewNote: Directs OSCA and the department of public safety, upon appropriation, to expend fund moneys on court automation and criminal history systems for expungement/sealing IT equipment, software, systems, services, personnel, or contractors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 610.144 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2 and corrected enactment citation to L. 2026 S.B. 1421) covering creation and investment of the Missouri Expungement Fund and authorized IT and personnel expenditures by OSCA and DPS (severability § 1.1010).

headings.title: Petition for expungement based on mistaken identity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a person named in a charge due to unauthorized identity use or mistaken identity whose charges were dismissed or acquitted to petition on an OSCA form for expungement after hearing, and mandates automatic court expungement upon prosecutor or judicial notice of dismissal.

headings.title: Protection from perjury or false statement liability
headings.reviewNote: Protects persons granted expungement under this section from perjury or false statement liability for failing to recite or acknowledge expunged apprehension, charge, or trial entries.

headings.title: Agency expungement directives, notice, and cost waiver
headings.reviewNote: Directs expungement from court, law enforcement, corrections, revenue, and other state or local agency records, requires clerk notice, and prohibits taxing expungement costs against the eligible person.

headings.title: Department of revenue expungement and license reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of revenue to expunge entries, reverse driver's license points, suspensions, or revocations, provide a certified corrected driver history at no cost, and reinstate affected licenses at no cost.

headings.title: Agency administrative reversal and reinstatement fee waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of corrections and other state or local agencies to expunge records, reverse resulting administrative actions, and waive normal license or privilege reinstatement fees.

headings.title: Three-year insurance premium refund for assessed points
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers that charged additional premiums based on insurance points from an expunged charge or conviction to refund three years of additional premiums upon notification and verification.

headings.title: Definition of mistaken identity
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'mistaken identity' as erroneous arrest resulting from witness or law enforcement misidentification, identity confusion, misinformation, or other mistake.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 610.145 (rewrote fabricated subsections 2 through 7 and corrected enactment citation to L. 2017 S.B. 34) covering stolen/mistaken identity expungement petition or automatic dismissal order, perjury immunity, agency expungement and cost waiver, DOR license reinstatement, corrections/agency reversal, three-year insurance refund, and mistaken identity definition.

headings.title: Confidentiality of deceased crime scene photographs and videos
headings.reviewNote: Closes crime scene photographs and video recordings depicting a deceased person in dismemberment, decapitation, mutilation, or exposed genitalia, while permitting access by defined next of kin (spouse, adult child, or parent) or with their written release.

headings.title: In camera review and public interest disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit judges in closed investigations to order image disclosure upon in camera review and written findings that public interest outweighs privacy.

headings.title: Mandatory two-week advance notice to next of kin
headings.reviewNote: Requires custodians to provide at least two weeks written notice to deceased next of kin prior to releasing crime scene photographs.

headings.title: Retroactive and prospective application to agency records
headings.reviewNote: Applies crime scene image confidentiality protections to all materials in agency custody on or after August 28, 2016.

headings.title: Exemption for criminal defense counsel and habeas proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Exempts defense counsel preparing appeals, new trial motions, or federal habeas petitions under 28 U.S.C. Section 2254 from disclosure restrictions.

headings.title: Public safety department rulemaking for credentialed press
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Department of Public Safety to promulgate administrative rules governing the viewing of crime scene images by credentialed media.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 610.205 (corrected subsection 1 title/note and enactment citation to L. 2016 S.B. 732) covering closed crime scene photographs/videos depicting mutilation or exposed genitalia, in camera judicial disclosure, two-week next-of-kin notice, agency custody applicability, defense/habeas counsel exception, and DPS press-viewing rules.

headings.title: Confidentiality of pending tax credit applications
headings.reviewNote: Deems records and documents submitted as part of tax credit applications to be closed records while applications remain pending and unauthorized.

headings.title: Disclosure of authorized credit records and redaction fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires disclosing nonexempt tax credit records upon request once authorized, with redaction of closed portions and section 610.026 staff-time fees (source footnote notes the 'all tax credit programs' definition in section 135.800 was repealed by H.B. 2400, 2022).

headings.title: Statutory definition of closed record
headings.reviewNote: Defines closed record for tax credit disclosure requests by referencing the general statutory definition under section 610.010.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 610.225 (added footnote on repealed § 135.800 definition) covering closed pending tax credit applications, disclosure and redaction fees upon authorization, and closed record definition (L. 2004 S.B. 1099 § 610.255).
